raw_response:
I have farmed here in Quzhou for 35 years, so I do not start from empty. I start from what worked on my land and then I adjust a little. I have 12 mu and only 2 people at home, so I cannot spread labor too thin. This year I will keep 6 mu in cotton, and I will use the other 6 mu for winter wheat followed by summer maize. That way I keep cash income from cotton, and I still have grain from the wheat-maize land. I have well water, so I will not be stingy with irrigation at key times, because if the crop gets held back once, it is hard to make up later. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than let yield drop. Cotton takes more careful feeding and more spraying, so I will give it the better land and more money. Wheat and maize I know well too, and around here many people use improved or hybrid seed now, so I will follow that. I will still keep rates close to what I know from past years, not make any big risky change.
